newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Puts traded in BAT following results.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Puts traded in BAT following results.

text.p: Stock options in B.A.T Industries attracted much trading interest on Wednesday following the company's first-half profits results, which were at the low end of analysts expectations.
Most of the activity was in put options, with the largest deal in the tobacco-to-insurance group coming from a buyer of 4,000 October 500 puts at 20p, dealers said.

One big seller of that series disposed of 3,000 lots at 19p-20p. B.A.T had earlier announced pre-tax profits for the six months to June 30 of 1.247 billion stg against analysts forecasts of between 1.237-1.301 billion stg.
B.A.T shares fell 21-1/2p to 518-1/2p by 1435 GMT.
Elsewhere, a long strangle was established in mobile 'phone company Vodafone, owing to the purchase of 250 January 300 puts at 18p as well as 250 January 330 calls at 15p.
For a profit by January expiry, the underlying shares need to either go below 267p or go above 363p.

There was mixed activity in the FTSE 100 index options as traders became wary of the market's current strength. Fearing a market fall, one trader bought 500 December 4925 puts in FTSE at 186p. Another trader bought 375 lots at 180p in the same series.
Another large deal was a calendar spread in FTSE, which involved selling 350 December 4925 calls at 245p and buying 350 March 4925 calls at 320-1/2p for a net debit of 75-1/2p.

At the December expiry, FTSE futures need to be at 4925 so that the spread will widen to its maximum amount because the short calls will then be worthless and the long calls worth more than 75-1/2p. The March calls will then be held if it is believed the market will rally.
By 1435 GMT, cash FTSE was up 44.2 at 4920.8, while September futures were up 45 points to 4943.
